construct: MOCS1 participates in the first step of molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis, converting GTP to cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate. Loss of molybdenum cofactor disables sulfite oxidase and other molybdoenzymes; sulfite accumulation is the major driver of severe neonatal neurotoxicity.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Neonatal encephalopathy with sulfite/S-sulfocysteine elevation, low uric acid, and biallelic MOCS1 variants identifies molybdenum cofactor deficiency. Severe neurotoxicity is driven by loss of sulfite oxidase and failure to oxidize sulfite to sulfate.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Homocysteine remethylation, methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, homogentisate oxidase, and phenylalanine hydroxylase use unrelated cofactors/pathways and do not explain sulfite accumulation.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Although multiple molybdoenzymes are impaired, the lead specifically asks which reaction explains neurotoxic sulfite accumulation, eliminating xanthine oxidase as a second valid Moco-dependent process.
